Counsel for Applicant :- Ravindra Kumar Patel,Ajay Tiwari,Ram Babu Tiwari
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Prashant Kumar Tripathi
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Case called out in revised list.
None present on behalf of the informant.
However, learned AGA for the State is present.

2. Heard Sri Ram Babu Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State.
3. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 553 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Koraon, District Prayagraj during pendency of the trial.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and two others on 27.12.2022 under Sections 363, 366 IPC and according to the FIR on 12.12.2022 applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 17 years with the help of co-accused Smt. Tara.

It is further mentioned in the Suresh Kumar Kushwaha vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67129565/
1 FIR that co-accused Smt. Tara with the help of the daughter of the informant also taken jewelries and money from the house of the informant.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and this fact is evident from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that from the perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. it appears that she compelled the applicant to take her and thereafter both have gone up to Sasaram, Bihar.
6. He further submits that from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it reflects that victim also performed marriage with the applicant according to her own sweet will.

7. He further submits that even as per school record at the time of incident victim was around 17 years and during investigation her ossification test was not conducted, therefore, at this stage,
precisely it cannot be said that victim was even below 18 years.
He further submits that even appearance wise victim looked like a major girl and it is a case of love affair.

8. He further submits that however applicant is having criminal history of one case relates to Section 147, 323, 504, 506 IPC but criminal history of the applicant has been explained in para-2 to the supplementary affidavit.
9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
11. However, from the school record victim appears that to be 17 years old but during investigation her ossification test was not conducted.

Further, in both the statements recorded during investigation victim did not make any allegation against the applicant and in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she categorically stated that she had already performed marriage with the applicant.
Further, victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. stated that on her compulsion applicant has taken her.

12. Further, however, applicant is having criminal history of single case but his criminal history has been explained in supplementary affidavit and it appears that it was of minor offences and applicant in the present matter is in jail since 28.12.2022 i.e. almost a year.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant - Suresh Kumar Kushwaha be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
